Whoever says the holes don’t line up or that it’s a “pain” to install, is wrong. This thing is as simple to put together as it gets, yes the hardware came in one bag & they were a bit oily. It took me maybe a minute to wipe them off & put them on a paper plate. When you get to the shelf, set the stand on its side makes it a lot easier to control. Unfortunately the bolts to attach my planer weren’t long enough, & the holes in the mdf didn’t match up so I drilled into it. No big deal to me as I can replace the top with some maple 3/4 plywood I have around the shop whenever I choose. The metal frame is really what we are paying for, & the casters too they are nice, 2 of them swivels & locks. I don’t understand people complaining that the pre drill holes don’t match their machine, you’re buying a “planer” stand. I’d assume you have the knowledge & tools to drill 4 holes lol. Just buy it already, it works great for the price.

I would gladly give this item 5 stars but the manufacturer ships these with only two pivoting casters with the other two being fixed. That makes too much humbug when trying to move this work table around. If I could find casters with the same mounting bolt pattern I'd get rid of the fixed casters on this item in a heart beat. The only reason I can see that the manufacturer decided to do this would be to save a few pennies. Really, a few pennies? The cart assembly is easy because everything lines up and fits.

If you've never bothered with a table for your drill press (mine is a Ridgid), this isn't a bad place to start. If you're thinking of making your own (as I was), from a cost perspective, I doubt you'd be able to buy all the parts included with this table separately, so you'd be ahead getting this simple table. Mind you the quality of the parts, while passable, are not the best. There are no features other than the sliding fence and stop which work OK. The clamps to hold the table to your drill press are kind of flimsy and require frequent tightening. I do find the table marginally useful though and maybe someday I'll still make my own... but I doubt it.
